operator_io_quirks: Backtick-quoted identifiers in DDL; generated SQL must double-quote ("City", "CountryCode") — sqlite accepts both, but writer must not copy backticks verbatim into INSERT.
Mixed-case table/column names (City, CountryCode, IsOfficial) — column lookup must be case-insensitive; keep original spelling in output.
CountryLanguage has composite PK (CountryCode, Language) — sample_fresh_primary_keys must dedupe on the tuple, not a single column.
Country.Capital is an INTEGER that semantically references City.ID but has NO declared FK — TS will not fill it consistently; it is a dangling logical FK.
CountryLanguage.CountryCode FK -> Country.Code, and Country.Code is TEXT PK; child draws from parent's FINAL filtered values (upstream order).
IsOfficial is TEXT with only 'T'/'F' (2 distinct) — String fuzzer will emit random charset strings, not T/F; no CHECK constraint to catch it.
IndepYear INTEGER with null_rate 0.197 and values like 1278 (implausible year) — Number fuzzer, not Date; no year semantics.
LifeExpectancy/GNPOld/GNP REAL nullable — Number fuzzer with scale from 'real' (no args) => default scale; nulls only via dropout, not NOT NULL enforcement.
Country.Capital nullable INTEGER, distinct 232 vs 239 rows — some NULLs; Number fuzzer will produce values outside City.ID range.
No views/triggers/indexes in DDL — writer clone is just 3 CREATE TABLEs; no extra objects to copy.
All tables small (4079/239/984) — no max_rows_per_table sampling needed; full read is cheap.
AUTOINCREMENT on City.ID — inserting explicit ID values is fine; sqlite_sequence not required for read-only units.
operator_ts_expectations: City.ID, Country.Population, Country.Capital, CountryLanguage.Percentage etc. -> Number fuzzer: uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] then +-1/+-2 perturbation; scale from type args (INTEGER/REAL have none => default).

City.Name, Country.Name, District, Region, Continent, GovernmentForm, HeadOfState, LocalName, Code2, Language -> String fuzzer: random a-zA-Z 0-9() strings length 0..20, plus 50% contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop char).

Country.Code, City.CountryCode, CountryLanguage.CountryCode -> String fuzzer but ALSO FK-filled from parent's final values (Country.Code / Country.Code) — so child values are plausible codes, not random strings.
CountryLanguage.IsOfficial -> String fuzzer random strings; original only T/F => TS will produce values like 'aB3' — likely FN driver (queries filtering IsOfficial='T' return wrong counts).
Country.Continent (7 distinct) and Region (25 distinct) -> String fuzzer random strings; queries grouping/filtering by continent get implausible values => FN.
Country.IndepYear -> Number fuzzer (INTEGER, no args) => uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale default; produces negative/huge years => FN on year-range predicates.
Country.Capital -> Number fuzzer, NOT FK-filled (no declared FK) => values unrelated to City.ID => joins Country.Capital=City.ID mostly empty => FN.

Composite PK (CountryCode,Language) dedupe keeps first occurrence; with random strings collisions rare => few drops; but FK CountryCode drawn from Country.Code (239 values) with replacement => many duplicate (code,lang) pairs possible if Language also repeats.
String fuzzer's contaminate (drop first/last char) on short codes like 'AFG' -> 'AF'/'FG' => breaks equality joins to Country.Code => FN.
Number fuzzer's list_max quirk (overwrites upper bound with full-range max) means even with literal pool, fresh draws span full range => implausible Population/SurfaceArea => FN.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python: rows violating NOT NULL (e.g. NULL in Name) fail at insert and are skipped => row counts shrink, possibly FP/FN on COUNT queries.
p=0.2 default, 30% chance whole instance p=0 => sometimes all values come from literal pool + 5 original samples => more plausible, fewer misses; variance across seeds.
